newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Apoyo puts Feb inflation at 0.01 pct.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Apoyo puts Feb inflation at 0.01 pct.

text.p: Peru's consumer prices rose just 0.01 percent in February, bringing inflation in the year's first two months to 0.88 percent, a leading polling and consulting firm said Tuesday.
Apoyo Consultoria SA's February inflation rate was even lower than the government's official figure of 0.09 percent for last month's rise in consumer prices, the lowest monthly inflation in 22 years.
Apoyo said in a statement that inflation in January reached 0.87 percent. It did not provide a figure for February 1995.
Last month's low rate was due mostly to a 0.95 percent decline in food prices, led by a plunge in chicken prices, which was offset by a 3.46 percent rise in educational services, Apoyo said.
The government's National Institute of Statistics and Information (INEI) reported over the weekend that Peru's inflation in February was low for roughly the same reasons.
By sector, food and beverages fell 0.89 percent, transport and communication slumped 0.14 percent and other goods and services dipped 0.11 percent, it said.

But Apoyo added other goods and services showed only modest rises. Clothing and footwear rose 0.25 percent; rent, fuel and electricity moved up 0.71 percent; furniture and household goods increased 0.51 percent; and recreation and educational services climbed 2.11 percent, it said.

Apoyo projected inflation will rise to between 0.8 percent and 1.0 percent in March due to higher educational costs, an expected adjustment in telephone rates and the impact of the Andean rainy season on the supply of agricultural products.
